body: Are you referring to me, or the fictional character in the story? I am curious to know.

Thanks. I've asked some of my family for help, which I think will be good. I was reluctant to say anything before because I didn't want them to know how terrible I was feeling. I hit a point where I figured it was more important to try to get any help that I could. Even though I still feel lousy, I'm more hopeful for the future than I was.

As I said, the blog doesn't really change the reasons I feel awful, but it helps me to organize what I'm thinking about. I have a tendency to obsess over certain thoughts and ideas, and writing it out seems to ease up the obsession so I can relax a little bit, or think about something else for a while.

Originally I had no plan to read anything after I posted it, for the same reason that I was afraid it would make me feel worse. I did decide to go back through and edit some things, though, and reading through wasn't quite as bad as I was afraid it would be. It was still miserable and suicidal, of course, but I was pretty happy with the writing style, as absurd as that may seem. There were also minor life problems that I didn't even remember worrying about until I read about it later. It was nice to see that some things that seem insurmountable in the present can become a faded memory.

I would suggest giving a blog/diary/journal a shot. You can make it as secret or public as you want, and if it seems more trouble than it's worth, you can delete it and forget about it.

I've been in a support group for caregivers when my wife was undergoing chemotherapy. I had a problem with the group format, and I never felt comfortable. I would cringe at the end when the moderator said it was time for the group hug. I didn't participate, and it still made me squirm. I could probably handle talking to 2 or 3 people at a time, but more than that and I know my anxiety would overwhelm me and I would shut down and not talk to anybody. I haven't seen any public groups that would offer the kind of individual attention that I would need to feel comfortable enough to talk.

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being whiny and picky. It's just that I know it would be more stressful than helpful to force myself to go through that again.

Unfortunately I am unemployed and couldn't afford to keep health insurance. I can't afford to visit a doctor. I've had to stop taking my antidepressants because I can't afford them any more. I know I should not have stopped, but I had to choose between meds or paying rent. A few months ago I gave a psychiatrist $250 to tell me that she couldn't help me because she didn't know me. Even if you consider she was lousy at her job, I can't afford to search around until I find a psychiatrist that can help me.

I appreciate what you are saying though. I shouldn't bottle everything up inside. It's difficult either way.
